owner: CC owns the charter corrections and the gate check. Akien owns the question of whether an at-rest component's absent journal is a red at all, or the ordinary state of a component between voyages — the answer changes what the check reds on, and it is not CC's to settle.
intention: A charter's present-tense claim about a file at its own address is checked against the address. Two halves, and the second is what makes the first stay true: (1) the seven chart-machine charters that assert 'state.json + history.json beside this charter. Both were born at the carve-out' are corrected to say what is true — the journal is born at this address's FIRST CROSSING, and until a ticket crosses here there is none; (2) the check that reds a charter naming a file beside it that is not there lands as a BUILD_INSPECTOR SIEVE — fired at every PROVEME crossing by physics — with bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate carrying the same predicate as the hand-run surface, so the next charter written by copying a sibling cannot inherit the falsehood silently.
why:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, and the measurement is small and total. Eight machines sit under cairn/devices/builder/machines/. Seven of their charters state in the present tense that state.json and history.json sit beside them; at seven of those seven, NEITHER FILE EXISTS. The eighth is orient, and its files did not exist either until this morning, when the orient-floor ticket crossed BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME -> PROVED and read_history's tolerance for an absent file created them on first append.

So the sentence is false twice over, and the second falsehood is the one that matters. It is not merely that the files are missing — the MECHANISM the sentence names is wrong. 'Born at the carve-out' describes a birth that has never happened at any of the eight addresses. What actually births a journal is a crossing, which is why orient's arrived weeks after its carve-out and the other seven's have not arrived at all. A reader trusting the charter would go looking for a record of the carve-out voyages and find nothing, and would have no way to tell whether the record was lost or was never written.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM: a Cairn mind stands in constrain/ to be briefed, reads that the machine's history is beside it, opens the directory, and finds no history. It now has to work out from first principles whether it is looking at a broken component, a lost record, or a component that has simply never sailed — and it has to do that at every one of the seven. That is Law 1's defect exactly: re-deriving a settled answer, seven times, because the artifact that should have carried it says something else.

WHY THE FIX IS NOT 'CREATE THE FILES'. An empty state.json at constrain would make the sentence true and the corpus worse: it manufactures a record of a voyage that did not happen, which is what Law 7 exists to forbid. The absence is HONEST. The charter is what is wrong.
traces_to: Law 5 — intent, its voyage, and its proofs share an address. A charter that misdescribes what is at its own address is the drift Law 5 is built to make impossible.
Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy. 'Do not assert a file that is not there' is prose in this ticket and stays a tracked debt until the derivation gate carries it.
Law 9 — red is the default. Seven charters currently read green about their own address because nothing derives the claim.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. The eight-address census is the measurement; before it, the claim was believed because it appeared in seven files.
gates: (1) The seven charters no longer assert a journal that is not there. What they say instead is a claim about the mechanism — the journal is born at the first crossing at this address — and it is TRUE of all eight, including orient, whose files arrived exactly that way. (2) The predicate — walk a charter, extract the filenames it asserts sit beside it, red any that is absent — lands as a build_inspector sieve, so it fires at EVERY PROVEME crossing without anyone remembering to run it (Law 4). bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate carries the same predicate for the hand-run corpus sweep; the sieve is the physics and the gate check is the surface. (3) The predicate reds TODAY on a deliberately malformed fixture and goes green on the corpus after (1) — a check that could only ever pass is the hollow build Law 8 refuses.
falsifier: RED if: (1) any of the seven charters still asserts state.json or history.json beside it while the file is absent; (2) the correction is made by creating empty journals rather than by correcting the sentence — that is manufacturing a record of a voyage that never sailed; (3) the new gate check passes on a fixture that asserts a file which is not there; (4) the check is written to look only for state.json and history.json — the defect is a charter asserting ANY file beside it, and narrowing it to the two filenames that happened to be wrong today is fitting the instrument to the sample; (5) the corrected sentence claims the journal will be born at the first crossing without that being true of orient, the one case where it can be checked against a real history.
horizon: After the chart floor build order Akien set on 2026-08-14 — orient, then constrain, then survey. This ticket was found WHILE building orient's floor and is deliberately not being fixed inside that build; but constrain and survey are two of the seven, so their charters are corrected as those stages are built, and the gate check lands with survey at the latest. Waiting past that means writing two more charters from a template known to be wrong.
dependencies: MEASURED, not assumed: the derivation gate already walks all 54 charters and already proves eight checks over them (bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate), so the ninth check needs no new traversal and no new reader — it needs a predicate. build_inspector already ran 20 sieves over orient at this morning's crossing, so the sieve side needs no new firing path either.

MEASURED 2026-08-14: nothing fires bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate automatically — it is hand-run. That is why half (2) lands as a sieve and not only as a gate check; a corpus check nobody runs is policy wearing a gate's clothes, which is the exact shape Law 4 calls an IOU.

OPEN, and Akien's: does an at-rest component's absent journal red at all? A component that has never sailed HAS no history, and that is its ordinary resting state, not a defect. This ticket's check therefore reds the CHARTER'S CLAIM, never the absence itself — but if the answer is that every component must have crossed at least once, the check is a different one and it is his to name.
distinctions_recorded: THE FILES ARE NOT THE DEFECT; THE SENTENCE IS. Seven missing journals at seven components that have never crossed is the correct state of the world. The charter describing that world wrongly is the only thing here that is broken, and the fix that creates files to match the prose would destroy the honest state to preserve the dishonest description.

THE MECHANISM IS WRONG, NOT JUST THE TENSE. 'Born at the carve-out' is not a true sentence waiting for its files — no journal has ever been born at a carve-out. orient's was born at its first crossing, weeks later, and that is the mechanism for all eight. Correcting only the tense ('will sit beside this charter') would leave the reader with a wrong model of when to expect the record.

HOW SEVEN CHARTERS CAME TO SAY THE SAME FALSE THING: each was written by copying a sibling. This is the same propagation already recorded at n=13 in the memory store — a wrong sentence in a charter is the template the next one is written from — and it is the reason half (2) is a gate check rather than seven edits. Seven edits fix the sample; the check fixes the mechanism.

WHY THIS DID NOT SURFACE UNTIL A TICKET CROSSED. The claim was unfalsifiable in practice: nothing read it, nothing derived it, and a reader who noticed the missing file had no way to tell it from a component between voyages. It surfaced only because orient's journal was BORN today and the contrast made the other seven legible — which is Law 9's shape exactly, a lot turning green one inspected piece at a time and the uninspected ones reading as whatever they last said about themselves.

SCOPE, and it was written into the wrong field at cast — moved here verbatim on 2026-08-14 when test_chart_notes redded it: 'The eight chart machines are where it was measured; the gate check is corpus-wide by construction and will find whatever else asserts a file beside itself. Expect it to red more than these seven on first run — that is the check working, and triaging its first harvest belongs to this ticket, not to a follow-on.' It was filed under chart_notes.scope, and `scope` is not a leg of the chart chain, so it was a note addressed to nobody. THE MOVE IS THE DISPOSITION THE NEW RULE NAMES: a deterministic red is fixed or carries a ruling, and the fix here is to put the prose where it is read rather than to loosen the leg check.
provenance: Born 2026-08-14 out of the orient-floor build, at the moment orient's history.json and state.json appeared under the PROVED crossing. The census that measured it: for each of the eight machines under cairn/devices/builder/machines/, test for state.json and history.json, and grep the charter for the assertion. Seven assert and have neither; orient asserts and now has both.

chart_notes.orient: The seven charters are cairn/devices/builder/machines/{constrain,decompose,hypothesize,survey,triage,validate,verdict}/intention+why.json, field state_and_history. The gate is bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate, whose checks live beside the map derivation; it currently proves eight over 54 charters. orient's journal, the one working example, is at cairn/devices/builder/machines/orient/{state,history}.json.

filed_edges: verdict's charter says something slightly different from the other six — it adds that the LEDGER is runtime state and lives in instance-space, never here. That clause is TRUE and must survive the correction; the fix is not a blanket replacement across seven files.

The same copy-from-a-sibling propagation almost certainly put other false present-tense claims in charters across the corpus. This ticket does not go looking for them by hand — the gate check is the instrument that finds them, which is why the check is half the ticket and not a nicety.
watchme: none, because the enforcement IS the standing instrument and a probe would be a second implementation of the same predicate — the re-derivation Law 1 refuses. After half (2) the sieve fires at every PROVEME crossing (cairn/machines/build_inspector/), so a charter that regains the defect reds a real voyage rather than a watch's counter. REFERENTS: bin/cmd/cairnmap --gate for the hand-run surface, and the PROVEME entry in cairn/devices/builder/machines/orient/history.json, whose sieve count lets a reader confirm the new sieve joined. NOT COVERED, stated rather than hidden: between this cast and half (2) landing, nothing watches — a window bounded by the horizon, which is why the horizon is a build-order position and not a date.
